property_summary: For any inputs where transfer is called, the reference contract C always returns true (call completes and returns true) because it invokes external transferFrom selector; the mutant that calls transfer(...) can invoke a function with a different return/behavior and thus can cause the overall call to either revert or return a different boolean for some adversarial callee — so the property is that calling transfer(...) on C never reverts and returns true for all admissible inputs, which the mutant can violate for some inputs.

For every admissible input, the reference C.transfer(...) always successfully completes and returns true (call does not revert and returns true); the mutant that calls a different selector can invoke a callee behavior that makes the overall call fail (revert) for some inputs, so the property is violated by that mutant.

For every admissible input, the reference C.transfer(...) always returns true (call completes successfully) even when the callee executes a function selector that does not revert; the mutant that changes the selector to transfer(...) can call a callee that deliberately reverts for that selector, causing the overall call to revert (breaking the property) for some inputs.

For every input where transfer is called with a non-empty _tos and a callee that enforces the third parameter is the token amount and the second is the recipient address, the reference forwards (from, to[i], v) to the callee and thus the callee sees amount==v and recipient==to[i]; the mutant swaps those two leading to at least some inputs where the callee observes a different amount/recipient (so the return from transfer differs) — we assert that calling transfer never reverts and returns true for the reference for all admissible inputs routed through an adversarial callee that requires (amount==v and recipient==to) but the mutant will sometimes fail that check.
